cards.title: Fasting or after food? It matters
cards.body: The same number means different things at different times. If the label is wrong, the doctor reads the whole log wrong.

cards.title: What fasting actually means
cards.body: No food for about eight hours, usually checked first thing in the morning. Water is generally fine. Follow any other instructions your doctor gives.

cards.title: After food means a fixed gap
cards.body: Your doctor will tell you how long after a meal to check. Use the same gap every time so readings can be compared.

cards.title: Clean hands, clean reading
cards.body: Wash and dry hands before pricking. Leftover sweets or fruit on the fingers can push a reading up. Use a fresh strip each time.

cards.title: Label every single reading
cards.body: Date, time, fasting or after which meal, and the number. 'Breakfast, two parathas' is honestly useful context to add.

cards.title: Targets come from the doctor
cards.body: Don't compare with a cousin's numbers or a forward in the family group. Your doctor sets the targets for your parent.

cards.title: Don't adjust medicine from the meter
cards.body: Readings help the doctor decide. Any change to tablets or insulin should come from the doctor. If something seems off, call them.

takeaway: Label every sugar reading as fasting or after food, keep the gap consistent, and let the doctor set targets and changes.
share: Sugar checks at home: fasting means about 8 hours without food. Label every reading.
